summary: This Apache web server configuration sets up a virtual host on port 80 that serves files from a specific directory. It enables URL rewriting to route all requests that don't match actual files to index.html, which is a common pattern for single-page applications. It also configures where to write error and access logs.

explanations.2: DocumentRoot tells Apache where the actual website files are stored on the server.
explanations.5: The Directory block applies specific rules only to requests for files in that particular folder.
explanations.6: AllowOverride All means Apache will respect .htaccess files if they exist in that directory.
explanations.7: RewriteEngine On activates Apache's URL rewriting feature, which lets you modify request paths before processing them.
explanations.8: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f is a condition that says 'only apply the next rule if the requested file doesn't actually exist on disk'.
explanations.9: RewriteRule ^(.*)$ index.html [QSA,L] redirects any request that matched the condition above to index.html instead, letting a front-end app handle routing. QSA preserves query parameters, and L means stop processing rules.
